<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via IObjectQLEngine (symbol, a top-level interface; a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via getObject (literal, a string literal in DataEngineLike))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via IObjectQLEngine (symbol, a top-level interface; a top-level type), judgeFilter (literal, a string literal in DataEngineLike))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), hasObjectMiddleware (literal, a string literal in DataEngineLike))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 81 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 523ada4cc0cf4308616249fd3364c630875a9c6e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a8003f81090313cb468e6de661f173d5f7705fe7` — the merge of head `978b92727c5c37b2618b2dd1c035ff3b3db3532a` into base `523ada4cc0cf4308616249fd3364c630875a9c6e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a8003f81090313cb468e6de661f173d5f7705fe7 && git checkout a8003f81090313cb468e6de661f173d5f7705fe7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 523ada4cc0cf4308616249fd3364c630875a9c6e 978b92727c5c37b2618b2dd1c035ff3b3db3532a && git checkout -B drift-repro 523ada4cc0cf4308616249fd3364c630875a9c6e && git merge --no-ff 978b92727c5c37b2618b2dd1c035ff3b3db3532a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 523ada4cc0cf4308616249fd3364c630875a9c6e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 523ada4cc0cf4308616249fd3364c630875a9c6e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The ruling allowed "about 3 to 5 lines"; this raises the limit by 3, which leaves #35773's +1. The registry row cites 7051956587. ✔
- **Deviation (b).** `IObjectQLEngine` is now imported from `@objectstack/spec/contracts`, not through core. Core's export at `index.ts:279` is the same spec type re-exported, so nothing diverges. Importing it from spec avoids the dual-chunk TS2416 error. Accepted. ✔

  - This is the right reading of the ruling's intent. Accepted. ✔
- **Pins.** All three run on the live SQLite harness:

  - (b) A real D4 class (`beforeFind` on `sys_record_share`): native declines, and the engine refuses 500.
  - (c) The member is absent: native declines, the engine path answers, and one warning is logged.
  - The wiring ablation (the config line removed) turns (a) and (c) red and leaves (b) green, as it should. ✔
- **Seat addendum: commits and hooks.**
  - All five commits carry only `Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` and `Claude-Session: …session_01L9qibwJEh7hMPPvagWM1g7`. No model name appears, and none of the messages has a closing keyword (`617f75327c`'s "resolves in" names no issue).

  - I cannot see from GitHub whether a hook ran locally. I can only confirm that nothing a hook enforces is missing.
  - The remaining lint lanes (ESLint, CI/release/engine, repo/tooling, docs/code guards, and the scoped lanes) were still running at my read. They re-run the same checks, so their green on this head closes the question.

### Owed (a record, no new head)

- **The fail-open mutant.** Deviation (a) is the PR's key safety argument, so pin (c) needs a positive control against exactly that form. Replace the plugin's `typeof` branch with `return svc.fixedReadLeafClassOf?.(leaf) ?? null;`. Pin (c) should go red: the native path compiles on an engine with no member. Post the red result and the clean restore.

### Landing conditions

1. **Deviation (c), a contradiction between two changesets.** #35945's changeset says "`AnalyticsServicePlugin` wires no answer in this release (#35946)". I asked for that clause in REWORK 7051798358, and it is true only if this PR ships in a later release.

   - Whichever lands second must make them agree. Either this PR, rebased after #35945 merges, rewrites that clause in `.changeset/35874-fixed-read-leaf-census-rest.md` (still pending, so editable), or #35945 words it conditionally before it lands.
   - The seat decides which; L1 only requires that no release carries both.
2. **CI green on `40fdd4e94e`** (24 checks in progress at my read). The dev ran 88 of 115 derived gate families locally and left the rest to CI.
3. **The CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2 PASS**, same head (`packages/spec/src/contracts/**`).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `40fdd4e94ec293ccb75729fb90c3dcca70b4d87b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts

PR #35954, card #35946, ruling 7051956587 (option A). The PR is stacked: its base is `claude/project-thread-thptm0` at `81da4605fa` (#35945's head, unmerged), which is also the merge-base, so the card's change is the 8-file diff `81da4605fa..40fdd4e94e` (+202 / -14). The diff against `main` also carries #35945's files; they were read as context and are not judged here. The rest of this diff (the test pin, the two generated spec baselines, the changeset, `scripts/facade-delegation-registry.json`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`IObjectQLEngine.fixedReadLeafClassOf?(leaf)` (new optional member)**: a widening of the public contract. Optional, so no implementer and no test double breaks. Right, and it is the member the ruling names.
- **`EngineFixedReadLeafClass` (new exported type, `@objectstack/spec/contracts`)**: a new public export. `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` each gain exactly that one row. Right.
- **`ObjectQL.fixedReadLeafClassOf` (new public method)**: additive. A one-line delegation to the seam's `fixedReadLeafClassOfEngine(this, leaf)`, the same recognition `passFixedReadLeaves` runs at the executor boundary (`fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts`). Right.
- **`engine.ts` now reads `IObjectQLEngine` from `@objectstack/spec/contracts`, not through `@objectstack/core`**: no change to what objectql publishes; core's re-export is untouched. Right.
- **`AnalyticsServicePlugin` accept set**: on a host whose `"data"` engine has the member, a read scope carrying a `SharedRecordIds` leaf outside both classes now takes the native SQL path (it declined on every host at the base). An engine without the member, no engine, a class answer and a throw decline as before. This is the widening the ruling orders, and nothing writes the leaf before step 6 (#33787). Right.
- **`DataEngineLike`**: its optional pick of `IObjectQLEngine` members gains this one; internal type, no surface. Right.
- **Facade ceiling** (`facade-delegation-registry.json`): `maxLines` 6854 to 6857, a raise of 3, inside the ruled "about 3 to 5". Measured: `engine.ts` is 6853 lines at `170ca481f0`, at `main` and at the base, and 6856 at the head. The row cites ruling 7051956587. Right.
- **Metadata protocol**: nothing an author can write changes. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/service-analytics`, the three packages the diff moves. `Clause-②: yes` is correct (a public surface widens: one optional contract member, one exported type, one engine method) and it stands on a line of its own in both the PR body and the changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: none` beside it. AGENTS.md: `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. No BREAKING banner is owed: the member is optional and nothing is removed. The level matches what the diff publishes.

Check-runs on the head, all converged: every run is `success` or `skipped`, none failed and none is pending. Among them: both `Check Changeset` runs, `Build Core` (the DTS build that the `engine.ts` import move answers), `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, every `Lint ·` job (`CI, release & engine gates`, `repo & tooling gates`, `PM dispatch-gates` among them), `Test Core` 10 of 10 shards, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness` and `Dogfood Regression Gate`.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` in the dev report (7052756244) is empty. The dev's declared deviations and out-of-scope findings, each answered:

- **The ruling's spelling `engine.fixedReadLeafClassOf?.(leaf) ?? null` is not used**: upheld. That spelling turns an absent member into `null`, which is the one answer `NativeSQLStrategy` compiles on (`classOf.call(ctx, leaf) !== null`), so it is fail-open. It contradicts the same card's facet ③ ("whose absence already declines fail-closed") and the ruling's own "ships unwired and declining fail-closed". The plugin's `typeof` probe keeps the ruled behaviour. See S1 for what this says about the contract's shape.
- **The contract's "neither" is `undefined`, because the facade gate refuses `?? null` in `engine.ts`**: not accepted as a reason for a published contract's shape. See S1.
- **`IObjectQLEngine` imported from spec instead of through core (TS2416 in the DTS build)**: accepted. The branded `FixedReadLeaf` is nominal per declaration copy, and spec ships a `.d.ts` and a `.d.mts`. The runtime side is safe: the brand is `Symbol.for(...)`. The type side is answered workspace-wide by `Build Core` and the three `Type Check ·` runs, all `success`; see ②.
- **The pin sits in the existing harness file**: the lane seat's; no contract effect.
- **Rebase and force-with-lease before the PR was opened; a commit attempt with `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` that the classifier denied**: the seat's to judge. No effect on the tree at this head.
- **Stacked PR, which AGENTS.md multi-agent section 2 marks unsupported**: escalated to the seat. This record names head `40fdd4e94e` over base `81da4605fa`. If #35945 lands in a way that moves this head (a squash followed by a rebase), this record no longer covers the result.
- **`.changeset/35874-fixed-read-leaf-census-rest.md` (#35945's) says "`AnalyticsServicePlugin` wires no answer in this release (#35946)"**: confirmed in the tree, line 16. Both PRs land before step 6, so they ship in one release and the sentence would publish false. It is a landing condition for the seat: the sentence is corrected in #35945 before it merges, or in this PR once it is retargeted to `main`. Not graded here: a changeset is outside ④.
- **Two declarations of the class type (`FixedReadLeafClass` in objectql, `EngineFixedReadLeafClass` in spec)**: see N1.

SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The change does the opposite: it lets the share-grant leaf stay one `IN (SELECT …)` subquery in the native statement where the host could not previously answer.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts` (hits), against ruling 7051956587, ADR-0155 D4 and its first consumer.**

Read against the live tree, the TSDoc holds sentence by sentence:
- "the engine seam's own recognition (`fixedReadLeafClassOfEngine`), the one the executor boundary runs": true. `passFixedReadLeaves` calls the same `fixedReadLeafClassOf(host, leaf)` over `securityResolversHost`.
- Both class descriptions match the seam's code (datasource binding of the leaf's object against the inner table's; `hasObjectMiddleware(table)` or a `beforeFind` / `afterFind` hook naming the table).
- "Read-only … calls no driver and logs nothing": true. `resolveDatasourceBinding` reads the registry, the mapping and the driver map; `hasObjectMiddleware` and the hook map are reads.
- "compiles only on `undefined`, and declines … on a class": true through the plugin's mapping to `null`.
- The header's "Five members are optional by ruling" list is correct for the member it adds.

D4's "restates none" holds: neither class is re-derived in spec or in analytics. Only the answer's type is stated in spec.

S1 (should-fix) — the member's "neither" answer is `undefined`, the same value an absent member gives through `?.()`, so the contract's two opposite answers are indistinguishable in the type and at run time for any caller that does not probe first.
- "Neither class" means "you may compile around the engine". "No member" means "cannot say, decline". These are the fail-open and fail-closed ends of a sharing-scope decision, and `ql.fixedReadLeafClassOf?.(leaf)` types both as `EngineFixedReadLeafClass | undefined`.
- The contract knows this: it carries a ⛔ against the natural spelling, and the ruling's own text wrote that spelling. A rule that the maintainer's ruling tripped on is one the next consumer trips on too.
- A second break: an engine that is not ObjectQL and implements the member as a stub returning nothing answers "neither", and the plugin compiles.
- With `null` for "neither" (`EngineFixedReadLeafClass | null`), `ql.fixedReadLeafClassOf?.(leaf)` is exactly the consumer hook's own three-state `FixedReadLeafClassAnswer` (class, `null`, `undefined`), the optional call is fail-closed by construction, a stub declines, and the ⛔ and the plugin's `?? null` both go.
- The stated reason for `undefined` is the facade gate's grammar in `engine.ts`. That is solved one file down (the seam's public face, or a sibling of it, answers `null`; `engine.ts` stays a one-line forward at the same line count). A tooling grammar should not set the shape of a published contract.
- Why now: the member is unreleased and has one consumer. After a release, changing the answer type is a breaking change to a published contract.
- Not a must-fix: the one consumer in this diff is correct and pinned, and the trap is documented.

N1 (nit) — `EngineFixedReadLeafClass`'s docblock says "`ObjectQL implements IObjectQLEngine` holds the two equal on every build". `implements` checks one direction only: the seam's answer must be assignable to the contract's. A class the seam adds fails the build (the direction that matters); a variant present only in spec, or a field the seam adds to a variant, passes. "Holds the seam's answer assignable to this type" is the accurate sentence. No effect on correctness.

N2 (nit) — the member's TSDoc does not say that it throws on a value that is not a fixed-read leaf (`fixedInnerReadOf` throws `TypeError`). The parameter is typed and the one consumer reads a throw as a decline, so nothing depends on it.

**`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (implementing).** The member is `return fixedReadLeafClassOfEngine(this, leaf)`, a forward and nothing else, so the contract's "the seam's own recognition" is literally true. Its return type is the seam's `FixedReadLeafClass`, checked against the contract by `implements`. The import move is type-only. Agrees with the contract as written. S1's fix touches this line's target, not its shape.

**`packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts` (implementing).** Read against the contract and against `NativeSQLStrategy.readScopeCarriesUncompilableFixedReadLeaf`, which compiles only on `=== null`:
- member present, answer `undefined`: `null`, compile. Member present, class: passed through, decline. Agrees.
- no `"data"` service, `getService` throws, member absent: `undefined`, decline. Fail-closed, as the contract's OPTIONAL paragraph requires.
- The member is called as a method on the service, so `this` is the engine; `ObjectQLPlugin` registers the `ObjectQL` instance itself as `"data"` (`objectql/src/plugin.ts`), so the production path reaches the member rather than the warn.
- A wrapper registered as `"data"` that does not forward the member, or one on which the host lookup throws, declines. A non-conforming answer (`false`, a promise) is not `null` and declines.
- The engine is resolved per call, like `hasObjectMiddleware`, so plugin order does not matter.
- The warn is once per plugin and names the remedy. It fires for an engine without the member, not when there is no engine at all; the changeset says the former, the PR body's sentence is broader than the code. The tree is right.
- No copy of either class. Agrees with D4.

The pin's three cases cover present-neither, present-class and absent through the plugin's real `init`. It reads the member through a plain object, so it pins the wiring and not `ObjectQL`'s method; the `implements` check and the delegation's single line cover that side.

Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibwJEh7hMPPvagWM1g7`

**VERDICT: PASS**
